raw_response:
I've been farming this land in Quzhou for over fifty years. My knees ache and my son went to work in Handan years ago, so it's just me and my wife now. We have 7 mu. I'm not going to try anything new at my age — I grow what I know, what my neighbors grow, what the soil here grows well.

Here, we all do the same thing: wheat in winter, corn in summer, same field, every year. The land isn't good for much else and I don't know anything else. The seed shop in town sells improved wheat — I'll get whatever they're pushing this year, probably Shimai or Jimai series. For corn I'll buy hybrid seed like I always do, Zhengdan 958 maybe, or whatever the dealer recommends. Hybrid corn gives more, everyone switched to it years ago.

For fertilizer, I put compound fertilizer down before planting and then urea when the crops are up. My son says I use too much urea but I'd rather be safe. A bad harvest and I can't cover costs. I pump water from the well — wheat needs water before winter sets in, again when it's jointing, and once more near harvest. Corn I water if the sky doesn't help me in July and August, and once when it's filling grain.

I can't plow myself anymore. I hire the machine operator from the village for rotary tillage before wheat. For corn I just direct-seed into the wheat stubble — no-till, saves me money and I don't have to wait.
